Product-Led vs Sales-Led vs Partner-Led Growth

Guidelowob research

By lowob · 22 May 2026 · 8-minute read · Strategy

Every company acquires customers through some combination of three motions: the product sells itself, people sell it, or other companies sell it. These are product-led, sales-led and partner-led growth. Most companies use more than one, but each needs a primary motion, because the three require different organisations. Choose the primary motion from how the buyer discovers, tries and buys the product, not from which one is cheapest, and add the others where they support it.

Every company acquires customers through some combination of three motions: the product sells itself, people sell it, or other companies sell it. The words for these are product-led, sales-led, and partner-led, and while most companies use more than one, each needs a primary motion, because the three require different organisations.

Product-led

The product is the main acquisition channel. People find it, try it free or cheaply, get value quickly, and pay to get more. Marketing drives sign-ups; the product does the convincing; sales, if it exists, arrives late to expand accounts.

It requires a product that delivers value without a conversation, a short time to that value, a price low enough to decide alone, and a buyer who can decide alone. It breaks when the product needs setup, integration, or trust before it is useful, when the buyer needs approval from others, or when the price is high enough to need a business case.

The economics are attractive: low cost per customer, high volume. The volume part is not optional. Kyle Poyar's summary of the investor OpenView's 2023 Product Benchmarks report, built with Pendo from more than 1,000 products, is a useful reference. Its illustrative funnel for an average freemium product has roughly 5% of new free sign-ups converting to paying customers. That is investor research from a self-selected sample, but it sets the scale: a product-led company needs about twenty sign-ups for each paying customer, and more if activation is weak.

The buyer side is pulling in two directions. Gartner's March 2026 survey of 646 B2B buyers found 67% preferred a rep-free buying experience, which favours self-serve. Forrester's State of Business Buying 2024 found an average of 13 people involved in a purchase decision and 89% of purchases involving two or more departments, which works against a buyer who can decide alone. The constraint is that it only works for products and buyers that fit, and many founders decide they are product-led because it is cheaper rather than because it is true. Our explainer What is product-led growth? covers the metrics in more detail.

Sales-led

People sell the product. Marketing generates and qualifies leads; sales runs a process from discovery to close; customer success keeps and expands the account. The product may be complex, expensive, or dependent on trust and configuration.

It requires a price high enough to pay for the sales cost, a buyer who expects a conversation, a repeatable process, and enough qualified demand to keep the team busy. It breaks when the price cannot carry the cost of selling, when the founder is the only person who can sell it, or when the pipeline depends on channels that have been closed to the category.

The economics are heavier and more predictable. The constraint is that it scales with headcount, and headcount is slow and expensive. The founder dependency is a separate failure, covered in Founder-led GTM is a job with an expiration date.

Partner-led

Other companies distribute the product: platforms that embed it, resellers, agencies, integration partners, affiliates, marketplaces. The company's own marketing and sales are aimed at partners as much as at end customers.

It requires a product that fits inside another company's offer, terms that make the partner money, and the patience to build relationships that take months to produce. It breaks when the partner's incentive is misaligned, when the company depends on one partner, or when the product needs more support than the partner can give.

The economics can be the best of the three once running: low marginal cost per customer, and distribution that no ad platform can revoke. Partners already hold much of the market. Canalys forecast in late 2024 that 70% of worldwide spending on technology, IT services and telecoms in 2025 would be delivered through partners, down from 73% in 2023. That is a forecast for the IT market as a whole, not for startups. Ebsta and Pavilion's 2024 benchmarks, vendor research across 530 companies, found partnership channels returned 3.8 times the deal velocity of outbound, inbound and paid channels, yet only 8% of the businesses studied had one. The constraint is time to first revenue, and the risk of concentration in a single partner. Our piece on partner channel design covers roles, payment and tiers.

Many founders decide they are product-led because it is cheaper rather than because it is true.

Why a primary motion matters

Each motion needs a different organisation. Product-led needs product, data, and growth engineering. Sales-led needs a sales team, enablement, and pipeline marketing. Partner-led needs partnership managers, programme terms, and partner marketing. A small company that tries to build all three builds none properly.

Choose the primary motion from the product and buyer, not from preference. Then add the others where they support it: sales to expand product-led accounts, partners to extend a sales-led company's reach, product-led onboarding to reduce a partner-led company's support burden.

Three questions about the buyer usually settle it. Can one person get value without help in the first session? Can that person pay without anyone else's approval? Does the buyer already buy adjacent products through someone else? Yes to the first two points to product-led; no to either points to sales-led; yes to the third makes partner-led worth testing early. Partners that bring customer overlap and introductions rather than resale are a variant covered in What is ecosystem-led growth?

For a company the platforms restrict

Restricted categories tilt the choice. Product-led motions that depend on cheap paid acquisition through the large platforms lose their main engine. Partner-led and sales-led motions, which run on relationships, affiliates, and channels that choose to carry the product, are less exposed. That is one reason affiliate and partner programmes are often the first thing worth building in these categories.

The restrictions are specific and change often. Google Ads, for example, requires advertisers of cryptocurrency exchanges and software wallets to be certified by Google and to meet local legal requirements country by country; its July 2025 update allowed certified advertisers targeting Canada if they were registered with the national money services regulator. A product-led plan built on search ads in that category depends on a certification process the company does not control. Our pieces on distribution when ad platforms restrict you and affiliate programs without coupon leaks cover the alternatives.

lowob takeaways

  • Choose one primary motion based on how buyers make decisions. Who gets value, who pays and who approves decide it.
  • Build the product and team to make that motion work. Each motion is a different organisation.
  • Check the economics against the benchmark. Product-led needs volume; sales-led needs price; partner-led needs patience.
  • Add other channels only where they reinforce the main path. Sales expands product-led accounts; partners extend a sales-led reach.

Common questions

What is the difference between product-led and sales-led growth?

In product-led growth the product does the convincing: people sign up, get value and pay without talking to anyone. In sales-led growth a salesperson runs the process from discovery to close, which suits complex, expensive or trust-dependent products.

What is partner-led growth?

A motion in which other companies distribute the product: platforms that embed it, resellers, agencies, integration partners, affiliates and marketplaces. It can have low marginal cost once running but takes months to produce revenue.

Can a company be both product-led and sales-led?

Yes, but one motion should be primary. A common pattern is product-led acquisition with sales arriving later to expand larger accounts.

What is a good free-to-paid conversion rate for product-led growth?

Benchmarks vary by model. An illustrative funnel from OpenView's 2023 study put roughly 5% of free sign-ups converting to paid for an average freemium product. Free-trial products are benchmarked separately.

  • Gartner, 67% of B2B buyers prefer a rep-free experience, 9 March 2026. Survey of 646 B2B buyers, August to September 2025; stated preference.
  • Forrester, The State Of Business Buying, 2024, 4 December 2024. Analyst press release; sample size not stated in the release.
  • Canalys, IT spending forecasts 2025. Analyst forecast, not actuals; covers the whole IT, services and telecoms market.
  • Ebsta and Pavilion, 2024 B2B Sales Benchmarks. Vendor analysis of 4.2 million opportunities at 530 companies; Ebsta sells sales software.
  • Google Ads, Updates to Cryptocurrencies and related products policy (July 2025), 1 July 2025. Platform policy page; policies change often, so check the current version.
